title: High-Pass Filter - Band 12 (700 MHz) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Ahmed Al-Farsi

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a High-Pass Filter filter targeting Band 12 (700 MHz) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter. The filter is designed on Quartz substrate with a target center frequency of 892.5 MHz and bandwidth of 361.0 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: High-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 12 (700 MHz)
- Application: GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
- Substrate: Quartz
- Package: Flip-Chip BGA
- Design Tool: CST Studio Suite 2024
- Design Center: Helsinki 5G Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the High-Pass Filter design targeting Band 12 (700 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       892.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       361.0 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.2 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 18.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 50.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 30.0 dB
Q Factor:               7370
Temperature Coefficient:-22.2 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.1 x 1.8 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   3
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open CST Studio Suite 2024 and load the High-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: Quartz with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 892.5 MHz, BW 361.0 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.2 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (Flip-Chip BGA).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, Quartz).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 2678 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.2 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 18.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 542 MHz offset >= 50.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 7 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 2.5 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +29 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 92%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-01-15
Devices Tested:         92
Insertion Loss (meas):  0.88 dB
Return Loss (meas):     19.7 dB
Rejection (meas):       52.9 dB
Isolation (meas):       35.1 dB
Q Factor (meas):        7370
Group Delay Variation:  3.2 ns
Power Handling:         +36 dBm
Die Yield:              94.2%

Result Classification:  FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The High-Pass Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 12 (700 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Optimize resonator geometry to reduce insertion loss by ~0.3 dB.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Escalate to advanced materials team for alternative piezoelectric stack.
